about: Built by tools/import-library.js from docs/research/exercise-library.md (batch L). The app embeds this file byte-for-byte. Edit the decisions in the tool, not this file.

newTags.shoulder_ir_elevated: The arm raised and turned in under load: upright rows to a high finish, bench dips.
newTags.elbow_flex_deep_loaded: The elbow deeply bent under load, as at the bottom of a skull crusher or overhead extension.
newTags.spine_rotation_loaded: Twisting the trunk under load: woodchops, landmine rotations, heavy one-arm rows with a twist.
newTags.adductor_lengthened_loaded: The inner thigh loaded at long length: wide stances, the adductor machine opened wide, Copenhagens.
newTags.neck_loaded: Load taken by the neck: neck curls and extensions, harness work, heavy shrugs.
newTags.knee_forward_loaded: Knees travelling far past the toes under load: sissy squats, step-ups and squats with the heels raised (a high load on the kneecap tendon).

iso_er.startDose: 5×30-45 s at a comfortable effort (about 30-50%), 1 min rest, daily
iso_er.progression: Increase effort 10% a week, then add positions
iso_er.advanceWhen: Pain ≤3/10 on resisted rotation tests; ER isometric pain-free

er_sidelying.startDose: 3×10-15, 2 s up/3 s down, alternate days
er_sidelying.advanceWhen: 3×15 at a set load, pain ≤3/10, 2 weeks

scaption.advanceWhen: Raise to shoulder height pain-free with load

er_90.condition: overhead/bench return; ER strength at end range
er_90.advanceWhen: ER strength ≥90% of the other side

landmine.advanceWhen: Landmine 3×10 @ about 40% bodyweight equivalent pain-free → incline DB

wrist_ext_iso.progression: Effort up, then switch to R12-R13
wrist_ext_iso.painNote: PR-T but keep effort below the level that raises pain (isometrics above pain threshold increased pain)
wrist_ext_iso.advanceWhen: Daily use pain ≤3/10; morning not worse

tyler_twist.progression: Next FlexBar colour after 3 weeks at 3×15
tyler_twist.advanceWhen: 3×15 on the heavier bar; grip pain ≤2/10

ecc_wrist_ext.advanceWhen: Pain-free gripping and lifting at work

pro_sup.condition: forearm rotators, elbow and wrist rehab
pro_sup.progression: Slide grip further up the handle

wrist_curl.advanceWhen: Pain-free bar holding in front squat or bench

wrist_wb.progression: Wall → bench → floor knees → floor; one step per week if pain-free
wrist_wb.advanceWhen: Full push-up position 30 s pain-free → push-up handles → flat floor

chin_nod.progression: Hold time to 10 s ×10, then lift head 1 cm
chin_nod.advanceWhen: 10×10 s without the front neck muscles taking over

prone_pressup.condition: LBP that eases with bending back
prone_pressup.painNote: PR-G; stop if leg symptoms move further down the leg
prone_pressup.advanceWhen: Centralising pain; can bend forward pain-free

sidelying_abd.startDose: Standing or lying iso abduction 5×30 s; then side-lying 3×10-15, daily → 3×/wk
sidelying_abd.progression: LEAP: iso week 1 → loaded functional (squat, step-up, side-step) wk 2-8
sidelying_abd.painNote: PR-G; avoid crossing legs and hanging on one hip
sidelying_abd.advanceWhen: Pain lying on side reduced; stairs ≤2/10

copenhagen.progression: Short → long lever; 1→3 sets; 3→15 reps over about 8 weeks
copenhagen.advanceWhen: 3×10 long lever pain-free; squeeze strength symmetric

spanish_squat.progression: Depth, then time, then add weight

peterson_stepup.advanceWhen: 20 cm step-down with good control, pain ≤2/10

pogo_hop.condition: tendon energy storage, return to jumping/running
pogo_hop.progression: Double → single leg → forward hops → bounds

rathleff_raise.startDose: 12RM×3 (wk1-2) → 10RM×4 → 8RM×5; 3 s up, 2 s hold, 3 s down; every 2nd day
rathleff_raise.progression: Add backpack load as reps get easy

balance_sl.advanceWhen: 60 s eyes closed; hop and stick
balance_sl.prehabDose: 2×30 s/leg in warm-up, 2-3×/wk for 12 months after a sprain

R10.name: Bench return ladder
R10.why: A return-to-bench ladder (floor press, then board or high pin, then paused full range), kept as ladder data for the rehab engine.

row.name: Bench return ladder
row.tissue_condition: return to bench after shoulder or pec pain
row.progression: Floor → 2-board/high pin → paused full ROM; one step every 1-2 weeks when PR-G holds
row.advance_when: Full-ROM paused bench at about 70% e1RM with no next-day flare
row.cues: Lower slowly;touch softly;stop at a pain-free depth

R16.name: Slow elbow flexion / extension
R16.why: The curl and the pushdown done slowly (3 s each way); logged on those with a tempo, not a separate exercise.

row.name: Slow elbow flexion / extension
row.advance_when: Old curl or pushdown weights pain-free
row.cues: Move slowly both ways;stop short of painful depth;keep shoulder still

R21.name: Rows and scapular endurance
R21.why: Rows, band rows and face pulls for neck pain; logged on those exercises.

row.name: Rows and scapular endurance
row.cues: Pull elbows back;squeeze shoulder blades;neck relaxed
row.sources: JOSPT 2017 neck CPG (neck and shoulder-girdle endurance, Grade B)

R24.name: McGill Big 3
R24.why: The McGill Big 3 is three exercises (curl-up, side plank, bird dog); side plank and bird dog are in the app, the curl-up is added (mcgill_curlup).

row.name: McGill Big 3
row.start_dose: Descending sets e.g. 6-4-2 × 10 s holds each, daily
row.progression: Add reps per set, not hold time
row.cues: Brace lightly like expecting a poke;hold still;breathe

R25.name: Walking programme
R25.why: A walking plan, not a lift; walking is an activity (batch N Part 3, quiet cardio).

row.name: Walking programme
row.cues: Walk at an easy pace;arms swinging;keep going even with mild ache
row.sources: Hayden 2021 (most exercise types beat minimal care)

R27.name: Hinge return ladder
R27.why: A return-to-deadlift ladder (dowel hinge, kettlebell deadlift, RDL, deadlift), kept as ladder data for the rehab engine.

row.name: Hinge return ladder
row.aliases: dowel hinge → KB deadlift → RDL → deadlift
row.progression: One rung every 1-2 weeks; load +5-10%/wk while PR-G holds
row.advance_when: Deadlift about 70-80% of old e1RM for 3×5, no next-day flare
row.setup: Dowel on back, then KB between feet
row.cues: Push hips back;keep chest proud;stand up by squeezing glutes

R38.name: HSR leg press / hack / squat
R38.why: Heavy slow resistance on the leg press, hack or squat (3 s each way, 15RM down to 6RM over 12 weeks); logged on those exercises with a tempo.

row.name: HSR leg press / hack / squat
row.start_dose: 4 sets, 15RM wk1 → 12RM wk2-3 → 10RM wk4-5 → 8RM wk6-8 → 6RM wk9-12; 3 s up/3 s down; 2-3 min rest; 3×/wk
row.progression: Load up as RM target drops (about weekly to biweekly)
row.cues: Lower for 3 s;push up for 3 s;no bounce
row.equipment_home_band: leg press (home: Smith or split squat)

R45.name: Seated + standing calf raise HSR
R45.why: Heavy slow seated and standing calf raises; logged on Seated and Standing calf raise with a tempo.

row.name: Seated + standing calf raise HSR
row.start_dose: 3-4×15 → 6RM over 12 weeks, 3 s up/3 s down, 3×/wk

R49.name: Achilles/calf return-to-run ladder
R49.why: A return-to-running plan, not a lift.

row.name: Achilles/calf return-to-run ladder
row.advance_when: Pain-free hop test; 30 min easy run
row.cues: Start easy and flat;keep pain within the rule;rest a day between runs
row.sources: Silbernagel 2007 (continued activity with pain monitoring = rest)

C030.name: Machine chest press
C030.why: The app has three machine chest presses (Converging chest press, Pin-loaded machine chest press, Lying neutral-grip plate-loaded chest press) and none is a seated plate-loaded iso-lateral press. Converging chest press is the likeliest, but it is selectorised.

V110.name: Iso-lateral chest press (one arm)
V110.why: Its parent (C030, machine chest press) has no certain match, so the one-arm version has no parent to sit under.

V148.name: Iso-lateral high row / pulldown
V148.why: The app has two plate-loaded pulldowns (Underhand plate-loaded lat pulldown, Single-arm plate lat pulldown); an iso-lateral high row could be either, or neither.

V181.name: Prone Y-raise
V181.why: Prone Y-raise could be the app's Low trap raise (below 90°) or a new exercise: a prone Y goes overhead, the app's low trap raise stays under 90°.

R06.name: Serratus wall slide / push-up plus
R06.why: Serratus wall slide and push-up plus: the push-up plus is close to the app's Scapular push-up and Serratus punch, the wall slide is neither. One row, three candidates.
